entries.title: N-Lex Malta national legislation discovery

cells: Use only as an EU discovery route for Maltese legislation; verify each result at LEĠIŻLAZZJONI MALTA. It is not a complete source inventory.

entries.title: LEĠIŻLAZZJONI MALTA official legislation portal

cells: Use as the official Malta legislation portal and route to published English and Maltese legislation. Select the displayed in-force/current record; this portal-level reference does not validate every instrument or its text.

entries.title: Free Movement of European Union Nationals and their Family Members Order, S.L. 460.17

cells: [Free Movement of European Union Nationals and their Family Members Order, S.L. 460.17](https://legislation.mt/eli/sl/460.17/eng)

Use the government-published English S.L. 460.17 text within its displayed amendment line (L.N. 107/2012 and Act XXIX/2019). It implements Directive 2004/38 for the scope stated in the Order; do not assume it covers every EEA/Swiss or Maltese-national route.

entries.title: Immigration Act, Chapter 217

cells: Use the official English Immigration Act, Cap. 217, within the portal’s displayed in-force record and amendment list. The Act is a framework source; read subsidiary legislation for specific procedures.

entries.title: Family Reunification Regulations, S.L. 217.06

cells: Use the official English S.L. 217.06 consolidation as the separate third-country-sponsor family-reunification route; its text identifies Directive 2003/86/EC and limits its scope to a third-country sponsor.

entries.title: Re-Use of Public Sector Information Act, Chapter 546

cells: [Re-Use of Public Sector Information Act, Chapter 546](https://legislation.mt/eli/cap/546/eng/pdf)
Use as the official Cap. 546 text only for public-sector information reuse context; it does not establish a blanket permission for every portal page, PDF, image or database.

entries.title: Working and residing in Malta: Identità operational guide

cells: [Working and residing in Malta: Identità operational guide](https://identita.gov.mt/working-residing-in-malta/)

Use the official external reference for Working and residing in Malta: Identità operational guide only, within its displayed publisher, language, version/date and stated subject. The combined EU/EEA/Swiss heading is a procedural description. Confirm legal route, treaty basis and family scope separately for each group.

entries.title: EU Nationals information hub

cells: Use the official external reference for EU Nationals information hub only, within its displayed publisher, language, version/date and stated subject. Parent page is a useful discovery index but its date and child membership need monitoring. Its permit/registration terminology should be reconciled with law and newer guidance.

entries.title: Registration certificate and eResidence document

cells: Use the official external reference for Registration certificate and eResidence document only, within its displayed publisher, language, version/date and stated subject. Use parent-page rediscovery and verify each live form/manual. The authenticated Expatriates Portal is not a public source-monitor target.

entries.title: EU national family member eResidence application

cells: Use the official Identità page for its published family application route and requirements only. Its category and evidence wording needs a legal crosswalk against S.L. 460.17 and Directive 2004/38; do not treat it as the complete eligibility rule.

entries.title: Exempt status for EU nationals related to Maltese citizens

Use the official external reference for Exempt status for EU nationals related to Maltese citizens only, within its displayed publisher, language, version/date and stated subject. A local exempt route differs from ordinary mobile-EU conditions and from family members of other EU citizens. Check exact statutory basis and changing document requirements.

entries.title: Right of appeal for EU-national free-movement decisions

cells: Use for Identità’s published EU-national appeal route only. The page points to S.L. 460.17 and the Immigration Appeals Board but does not give a complete deadline/remedy map.
